title: seccomp: socketpair is not restricted by address family, so any family's kernel module can be autoloaded
body:
The default profile allows socketpair(2) unconditionally. Only AF_UNIX and AF_TIPC implement it, so for any other family the call can only fail. Before failing, though, the kernel tries to create the socket, which can autoload that family's module. I propose allowing socketpair only for those two families.

  Reproducer

```
  $ sudo mv /etc/modprobe.d/rds-blacklist.conf{,-}

  $ lsmod | grep rds

  $ sudo podman run --rm docker.io/library/python \
      python3 -c "import socket; socket.socketpair(socket.AF_RDS, socket.SOCK_STREAM)"
  OSError: [Errno 94] Socket type not supported      <confirm on main's profile>

  $ lsmod | grep rds
  rds                   176128  0
```

  With the proposed change the same command fails with `OSError: [Errno 38] Function not implemented`, because denied syscalls get the profile's default ENOSYS.

  Proposed change

  Remove socketpair from the unconditional allow list and allow it only when argument 0 is AF_UNIX (1) or AF_TIPC (30). The rules are plain equality checks, so a value with upper bits set doesn't match.

  Caveats

  - On ABIs that use socketcall(2) the arguments are behind a pointer, so this can't be filtered there. socket has the same limitation.
  - Calls with any other family will now fail with ENOSYS instead of ESOCKTNOSUPPORT or EAFNOSUPPORT. Nothing legitimate should be affected, since those calls can't succeed anyway.
